sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define stress according to Hans Selye.
questions.answer: A non-specific response of the body to any demand on it.

questions.q: Name the two categories of stress.
Name the four categories of stressors.
questions.answer: Major life events and changes, daily hassles, chronic role strain and traumas.

questions.q: Name the three types of conflict.
Define frustration.
questions.answer: An experiential state resulting from blocking of needs and motives by external forces or the absence of a desired goal.

questions.q: Name any two anxiety disorders.
Name the two mood disorders.
Differentiate psychosomatic and somatoform disorders in one line.
questions.answer: Psychosomatic: physical symptoms with psychological causes; somatoform: physical symptoms with no identifiable biological cause.

questions.q: Name any two dissociative disorders.
questions.answer: Dissociative amnesia, dissociative fugue, depersonalization disorder, multiple personality disorder (any two).

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Identify the stressor category: (i) divorce; (ii) misplacing items; (iii) living in poverty; (iv) death of a loved one.
questions.answer: (i) Major life event. (ii) Daily hassle. (iii) Chronic role strain. (iv) Trauma.

questions.q: Name the conflict: (i) two desirable invitations on the same night; (ii) unemployment or a disagreeable job; (iii) wanting to marry but fearing responsibilities; (iv) which is called a mixed-blessing conflict?
Name the coping type: (i) planning revision for a tough test; (ii) leaving a rejecting friend and making a new one; (iii) accepting a substitute goal; (iv) blaming a tough paper for failure.
Write the steps of psychotherapy in order (first four).
questions.answer: Rapport formation; preparation of case history; determination of the problem; therapeutic sessions (then termination).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: Differentiate eustress and distress with examples.
questions.answer: Eustress is moderate desirable stress such as playing a competitive sport; distress is excessive, undesirable stress.

questions.q: What are daily hassles? Give two examples.
questions.answer: Irritating, frustrating demands of everyday life such as deadlines and traffic jams.

questions.q: What is an approach–avoidance conflict?
questions.answer: A strong tendency both to approach and to avoid the same goal, e.g. wanting to marry yet fearing loss of freedom.

questions.q: What is ADHD?
questions.answer: Attention-deficit hyperactive disorder: a childhood disorder with difficulty paying attention and extreme over-activity.

questions.q: What is depression?
questions.answer: A mental state of sadness, loss of interest, sleep and appetite disturbance, guilt and hopelessness lasting at least two weeks.

questions.q: What is multiple personality disorder?
questions.answer: A serious dissociative disorder in which several distinct personalities emerge in the same person at different times.

questions.q: Who is a psychiatrist?
questions.answer: A medical doctor specialised in mental disorders who can prescribe medicines.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the recent approach to stress.
questions.answer: It focuses on appraisal of a situation in relation to the person's coping resources; appraisal and coping determine adaptation, the management of the environment to maintain well-being.

questions.q: Describe the types of stressors.
questions.answer: Major life events (marriage, retirement), daily hassles (deadlines), chronic role strain (difficult marriage, poverty) and traumas (bomb blast, death of a loved one).

questions.q: Explain the types of conflict with examples.
questions.answer: Approach–approach between two desirable goals; avoidance–avoidance between two undesirable goals; approach–avoidance with attraction and fear of the same goal.

questions.q: Describe schizophrenia.
questions.answer: A disorder of thought, emotion and behaviour: incoherent thinking, faulty perception, disturbed movement, flat or inappropriate emotions and withdrawal into delusions and hallucinations.

questions.q: Explain the steps in psychotherapy.
questions.answer: Rapport formation, case history, determination of the problem, therapeutic sessions with progress monitoring and termination of intervention with follow-up advice.

questions.q: Distinguish task-oriented and defence-oriented coping.
questions.answer: Task-oriented coping is rational and constructive (attack, withdrawal, compromise); defence-oriented coping makes one feel comfortable without solving the problem (rationalisation, displacement).

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Define stress and discuss the stressors and responses to them.
questions.answer: Stress is a non-specific response of the body to demands (Selye): eustress and distress. Stressors: major life events, daily hassles, chronic role strain and traumas. Responses: behavioural, emotional, cognitive, interpersonal, biological and imagery.

questions.q: Explain how conflict and frustration lead to stress.
questions.answer: Obstacles to goals cause conflict (approach–approach, avoidance–avoidance, approach–avoidance) and frustration from blocked needs or absent goals, caused by physical and social hindrances and personal limits; their intensity makes them stressful.

questions.q: Describe any five mental disorders and their symptoms.
questions.answer: Anxiety (phobia, OCD), mood (depression, bipolar), psychosomatic and somatoform, dissociative (amnesia, fugue, depersonalization, multiple personality), schizophrenia (delusions, hallucinations), childhood (ADHD, autism) and personality disorders in three clusters.

questions.q: Discuss the psychotherapeutic process and the desirable ways of coping with stress.
questions.answer: Psychotherapy by a clinical psychologist follows rapport, case history, problem identification, sessions and termination; approaches include psychoanalysis, behaviour, cognitive-behaviour and client-centred therapy. Coping: attack, withdrawal and compromise, avoiding defence mechanisms, with a healthy life-style and positive thinking.
